+# description: MERGE with WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE and a subquery in ON that is correlated with the source
+CREATE TABLE t (id INT PRIMARY KEY, v INT);
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id) WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id AND s.v > (SELECT min(s2.v) - 1 FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id)
+WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v = s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET v = 0;
+# several source rows, for which the subquery decides differently, and all three kinds of actions
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id AND s2.v > 20)
+WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v = s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE
+WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (s.id + 100, s.v);
+# a correlated subquery in an action, and one nested in another in the join condition
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id
+WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v = (SELECT count(*) FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id <= s.id) WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id
+AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s s3 WHERE s3.v = s.v AND s3.v > 20))
+WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;
+# a correlated subquery in the condition of an action
+MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id
+WHEN MATCHED AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id AND s2.v > 20) THEN UPDATE SET v = -1
+WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;

+# description: A macro parameter passed as a named argument is the macro parameter, whatever the argument is named
+CREATE MACRO pivot_first(x) AS TABLE PIVOT (SELECT 1 k) ON k IN (1) USING first(struct_pack(a := x));
+# the argument has the name of a lambda parameter, the value is the macro parameter
+CREATE MACRO pack_parameter(y) AS list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(x := y));
+# description: A lambda parameter passed as a named argument is the lambda parameter, not a column of the same name
+SELECT list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x)) FROM tt
+CREATE MACRO m(x) AS list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x));
+# the aggregate belongs to the subquery, not to the query with the column of the same name
+SELECT (SELECT max(list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x))[2].a) FROM range(3)) FROM tt
+SELECT (SELECT count(*) + max(list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x))[2].a) FROM range(3)) FROM tt
+SELECT r FROM tt, LATERAL (SELECT max(list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x))[2].a) AS r FROM range(3))
+CREATE TABLE up (k INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, x INTEGER, l STRUCT(a INTEGER)[]);
+INSERT INTO up VALUES (1, 20, NULL) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET l = list_transform([1, 2], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x));
+CREATE TABLE ck (x INTEGER, CHECK (list_transform([x], lambda x: struct_pack(a := x)) IS NOT NULL));
+Lambda functions are currently not supported in CHECK constraints
+# the argument has the name of the lambda parameter, the value is the column
+CREATE TABLE ck_column (y INTEGER, CHECK (list_transform([1], lambda x: struct_pack(x := y)) = [{'x': 5}]));
+Lambda functions are currently not supported in CHECK constraints
+# a column captured by a lambda is not supported either
+CREATE TABLE ck_capture (y INTEGER, CHECK (list_transform([7], lambda x: y) = [7]));
+Lambda functions are currently not supported in CHECK constraints
+CREATE TABLE ck_qualified (z INTEGER, y INTEGER, CHECK (list_transform([7], lambda x: ck_qualified.y) = [5]));
+Lambda functions are currently not supported in CHECK constraints
+# a lambda that references neither stays supported
+CREATE TABLE ck_constant (y INTEGER, CHECK (list_transform([y], lambda x: 7) = [7]), CHECK (y > 0));
